carmen: Heads up — ran a small repro on staging and hit a weird invariant after a shard reassign. Tenant A ended up with two 'resident' entries for the same prefix, eviction counters diverged, and we dropped requests for ~30s.

carmen: minimal log snip:
```
[2026-02-10T21:02:11Z] stash: assign shard s42 -> node-7
[2026-02-10T21:02:12Z] evict: mark resident prefix/tenantA/abc (slot 12)
[2026-02-10T21:02:12Z] evict: mark resident prefix/tenantA/abc (slot 34)
[2026-02-10T21:02:40Z] request: tenantA read prefix/abc -> miss / 503
```

carmen: repro steps in case you want to run it: 1) create 2 concurrent handoffs for hot prefix 2) trigger a small eviction churn 3) rapidly ping read route.

tom: cc @carmen — can you paste the handoff sequencing? was this a split or a reassignment (not demote)?

carmen: it was reassignment (node-7 -> node-3). not a split. the two mark-resident lines come from different nodes during the overlap window.

tom: ah ok. sounds like we might be double-claiming when the demote -> claim overlap doesn't clear old residency. quick Q: are we using epoch CAS on the residency metadata today?

kevin: currently residency uses (owner_id, generation) where generation is counter but we only CAS on owner_id. generation is set by owner after claim.

kevin: so during a fast handoff the old owner can still set generation that looks newer to some observers — race.

sasha: yikes. that's exactly one of the scenarios we flagged in the bounded-handoff RFC but assumed soft-evict would mask it. clearly not here.

sasha: two approaches:
- add monotonic epoch that only claim path increments and is CASed atomically
- or include a short-lived reservation cookie tied to claim RPC that other nodes must check and respect

kevin: epoch CAS seems cleaner but requires an extra store field and slightly more writes on every claim. reservation cookie is lighter but more protocol-y.

tom: does reservation cookie buy us anything for existing demote flows? i.e., can old owner still erroneously re-mark after demote? cookie would be invalidated on demote ack.

carmen: in my run the old owner was asynchronous and re-marked because it retried a pre-demote write — cookie would've prevented that.

kevin: prototype idea for epoch CAS:
```
// on claim
expected = read(metadata.epoch)
if CAS(metadata.epoch, expected, expected+1) {
  set owner=nodeX
  set resident=true
}
```
reads check metadata.epoch >= local_seen_epoch
```

kevin: downside: every claim bumps epoch so very chatty handoffs slightly increase write volume.

sasha: tradeoff: epoch simplifies correctness proof and lets us reuse existing lease/epoch counters in the runtime. cost is writes but claims are relatively rare compared to reads.

tom: operational question: how will this look in metrics? we need a clear signal during canary.

kevin: add evict.epoch_mismatch_counter, evict.double_residency_gauge, and handoff.claim_rps. Also log claim epochs in trace spans.

evict-bot: new metric asked: evict.double_residency_gauge created (user=kevin, id=EVICT-314)

carmen: agree. propose plan:
1) small runtime patch that CASes epoch (kevin will proto)
2) unit + deterministic sim test for concurrent handoff
a) simulate interleaved demote/claim/retry
3) canary on 10% of shards with metrics gated
4) rollback knob if double_residency > 0 after 5m

sasha: add a safety step: if a claim sees an epoch jump > 1, emit a debug dump to S3 (short term) so we can inspect interleavings.

tom: sounds good. @kevin want to own the proto and the sim? i can take canary rollout and alerts.

kevin: can do. will open a tiny PR and a sim harness test by EOD tomorrow.

carmen: thanks! I'll attach the repro script to the PR and run it during canary.

kevin: one last thing — do we need to plumb this through Dedicated/Private differences? naming of metadata keys might need to be backward compatible for rolling upgrades.

sasha: keep the new epoch field optional (default 0). ops path will flip node agents to start using CAS after half of cluster upgraded. add compatibility note in PR.

carmen: perfect. creating tracking ticket now: GH#5212. linking in PR once open. :thumbsup:

tom: thanks all. catching up in sync if anything weird shows up during canary.

kevin: FYI I'll also add a quick telemetry flag to suppress noisy debug dumps after 1hr if it's a noisy canary.

carmen: noted — last_message: repro attached to GH#5212. will update thread.
